Senses.PreferredTarget: originally, there is not a single thing
AlternateTargets: from the first, there is not one thing
Senses.Explanation: Originally, there is not even one thing: ‘originally’ (本來) places the denial at the root or beginning, while ‘not a single thing’ (無一物) makes it exhaustive. The phrase occurs 214 times in 106 allowlisted texts, with a contracted form appearing 34 times in 30. It is the third line of Huineng's verse in the received Zongbao edition of the Platform Sutra: ‘Bodhi originally has no tree; the bright mirror is also not a stand. Originally, there is not a single thing—where could it attract dust?’ (菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺；本來無一物，何處惹塵埃). This wording belongs to that later received textual line: the Dunhuang Platform Sutra instead reads, ‘Buddha-nature is always pure—where could there be dust?’ (佛性常清淨，何處有塵埃), without the headword. Lamp collections transmit variants such as ‘where could there be dust?’ (何處有塵埃) and ‘why rely on wiping away dust?’ (何假拂塵埃). The records do not leave the phrase as an uncontested slogan. Dongshan Liangjie says that even directly declaring it has not earned the robe and bowl, while Huangbo Xiyun answers an unnamed questioner who asks whether ‘no-thing’ is it: ‘Even “no” is not it’ (無亦不是). Yulin Tongxiu later raises Huineng's line beside Changqing's ‘the solitary body is exposed amid the myriad phenomena’ (萬象之中獨露身). Its Chan deployment is therefore a named verse-line repeatedly transmitted, contrasted, and publicly tested; the entry states its grammar and those uses without deciding what metaphysical theory the line finally proves.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide verse-line sense. The received Platform Sutra explicitly presents the verse as Huineng's, using an alternate graph in his written name. The Jade Blossoms of Lamp Transmission variant belongs to the same robe-transmission episode and is likewise attributed to Huineng. The Patriarchs' Hall Collection and Jade Blossoms independently preserve Dongshan Liangjie's critical verdict. Huangbo Xiyun owns the question-and-answer exchange in his Wanling Record. In Yulin Tongxiu's later raising, Huineng remains the quoted speaker of the line and Yulin is recorded as the quoter. The Dunhuang reading is retained solely as a labelled contrast occurrence and does not count as headword depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺；本來無一物，何處惹塵埃？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The received Zongbao edition of the Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經), in the first section, explicitly introduces this as Huineng's verse (惠能偈曰). Huineng's third line says, ‘Originally, there is not a single thing,’ followed by ‘where could it attract dust?’

Occurrences.Kwic: 本非樹心鏡亦非臺本來無一物何假拂塵埃
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Fragmentary Jade Blossoms of Lamp Transmission (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), in Hongren's robe-transmission chapter, says that Huineng had a boy write this verse beside Shenxiu's. It preserves the variants ‘Bodhi originally is not a tree’ (菩提本非樹) and ‘why rely on wiping away dust?’ (何假拂塵埃).

Occurrences.Kwic: 身非菩提樹，心鏡亦非臺。本來無一物，何處有塵埃？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集) narrates Huineng asking Zhang Riyong to write down his understanding and then presents the verse Zhang writes for him. This witness begins ‘the body is not the bodhi tree’ and ends ‘where could there be dust?’

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山答曰：「直道本來無一物，也未得衣缽在。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), in Dongshan Liangjie's section, explicitly marks Dongshan's answer. Asked why Shenxiu's ‘wipe it diligently at all times’ did not win the robe, Dongshan says that even directly declaring ‘originally, there is not a single thing’ has not earned the robe and bowl.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師有時垂語曰直道本來無一物猶未消得佗鉢袋子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Fragmentary Jade Blossoms of Lamp Transmission (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), in Dongshan Liangjie's section, says that Dongshan sometimes offered this statement: even directly declaring the line has not yet merited the other's bowl-bag. This is an independent witness to Dongshan's verdict.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問本來無一物無物便是否師云無亦不是菩提無是處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Wanling Record of Huangbo Xiyun within the Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄) records a monk asking whether, if originally there is not one thing, ‘no-thing’ is it. Huangbo answers, ‘Even “no” is not it.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉六祖云本來無一物長慶云萬象之中獨露身
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄) records Yulin Tongxiu raising Huineng's ‘originally, there is not a single thing’ beside Changqing's ‘the solitary body is exposed amid the myriad phenomena.’ Huineng is the explicitly named quoted speaker; Yulin owns the act of raising and the following comment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 將他本來無一物之語，以情意識和會卜度，便道無三界可出，無涅槃可證
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Miscellaneous Records of Chan Master Tianmu Mingben (天目明本禪師雜錄): Zhongfeng Mingben warns against using discriminating consciousness to calculate over the saying 'originally not one thing' and drawing further conclusions from it.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 佛性常清淨，何處有塵埃
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 惠能偈曰：「菩提本無樹，明鏡亦無臺，佛性常清淨，何處有塵埃？」
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: The Dunhuang Platform Sutra (南宗頓教最上大乘摩訶般若波羅蜜經六祖惠能大師於韶州大梵寺施法壇經) explicitly introduces this as Huineng's verse (惠能偈曰); Huineng utters the alternate verse line quoted here.
